public_rationale: The available supplier disclosures do not reproduce Zitron's market total. CoreWeave's total revenue cannot be treated as eligible revenue without the customer and service exclusions. Lambda's cited estimate is annualized and cannot be added as realized 2025 revenue. Neither a complete total below $1 billion nor a reliable eligible lower bound of at least $1 billion was established. The accompanying percentage also lacks a defined denominator.
limitations: The market includes private suppliers with limited financial disclosure.
Supplier totals and customer exclusions require reconciliation.
Alternative definitions of hyperscaler and AI-compute services could change the aggregate.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Excluding hyperscaler and OpenAI contracts, AI compute revenue in 2025 was under $1 billion.

statement.excerpt: Otherwise, when you remove the contracts signed by hyperscalers and OpenAI (which I do not believe has paid anybody other than Microsoft yet), based on my analysis, there was less than a billion dollars of AI compute revenue in 2025, or 0.5831% of the money spent on data centers.

our_interpretation: The assessed threshold is realized AI-compute rental revenue below USD 1 billion during calendar 2025.
I read the exclusion as removing transactions in which hyperscalers or OpenAI purchase compute, rather than removing every sale by a supplier that also serves those customers.
Hyperscalers includes large-scale operators such as Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle; borderline classifications must be disclosed and tested for sensitivity.
The customer exclusion is a market-definition rule, not a conditional forecast.
The full calendar year follows the explicit wording in 2025, although the post appeared two days before year-end.
The accompanying percentage requires a separately defined data-center-spending denominator. It cannot be verified from the revenue threshold alone.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently complete, consistently defined estimate places eligible realized 2025 AI-compute rental revenue below USD 1 billion. Verification of the accompanying percentage additionally requires a matching spending denominator.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A same-scope market estimate, or a documented non-overlapping lower bound, establishes eligible realized 2025 revenue of at least USD 1 billion.

evidence.explanation: The filing reports $5.131 billion of total 2025 revenue and approximately 67% from Microsoft. Those figures do not isolate eligible AI-compute revenue after removing OpenAI, other hyperscalers and any nonqualifying services.
This is an annualized year-end estimate, not realized calendar-year rental revenue. It also does not remove hyperscaler and OpenAI purchases, so it cannot be added to a qualifying market total.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reconciled 2025 supplier-by-customer revenue dataset, or a documented eligible lower bound of at least $1 billion, using consistent revenue recognition and exclusions. The percentage also requires its spending denominator.
